Thanks to @delta shortcomings as an airline tonight, I find myself in market longer than expected. So with time to kill, I made my way up Park Avenue to Park Avenue Tavern. Took a seat at the bar and ordered up the Park Tavern Burger. Medium. Bacon. Cheddar. $27 with fries included of course. Maybe it was my outrage at certain commercial airliners, but I was caught off guard. I was expecting the usual, but what I got was far from it. It was a classic. Served promptly a mere 9 minutes after I placed the order. Cooked to perfection on a nice sesame seed brioche bun. $27? Undervalued surprisingly. I price this burger up there with the $30 guys. 8.15/10. Strong BUY.
Side note: The young gentleman on the presumable Hinge date to the left of me could learn a lesson in what nice ladies want to hear you ramble about. Collegiate lacrosse injuries, bar fights, and your boss that’s “[your] boy” are not it.  We’ll be out of market starting tomorrow through the rest of the weekend. Thank you @united for solving the problem.

1963 press photo of Alex “Shondor” Birns. Born February 21, 1905, and assassinated by Car bomb March 29,1975 due to a dispute with local Irish gangster and FBI informant Danny Greene. He started off stealing cars and other petty crimes when he was a young man and racked up around 20 arrests in a 12 year time span but was only prosecuted a couple times. Shondor is eventually recruited by Maxie Diamond the leader of the E. 55th street and Woodland Mob as a collector, he was very active in a war for control over the city’s dry cleaning and laundering rackets. In 1934 Shondor got into a dispute with a bouncer at a club named Rudy Duncan, they got into a physical altercation, guns came out and shots were fired.Shondor and his gang were kicked out of the club and arrested, but 2 months later Shondor got revenge when Duncan and his foster son went out for a movie and ice cream, Duncan was shot 5 times and died, the case is still unsolved. During the 1930’s Shondor began working with the Cleveland  crime family in  prostitution,extortion, collections, etc. eventually he would open multiple legitimate businesses including his “Ten - Eleven Club”. In the 1960’s he would hire Danny Greene to be an enforcer/ collector. 1976 Cleveland Don John Scalish died during heart surgery and there was no clear boss named, but Jack “white” Licavoli ended up with the position. Total chaos broke out in the Cleveland underworld and there would be bombs going off almost every other day, everyone was fighting for control and Shondor would become a victim of this war. Danny Greene would also find himself blown up by a car bomb on October 6, 1977. The Danny Greene war bassicly destroyed traditional organized crime in the area.
